purpose: Cross-genre reusable video resource library: bundle original assets and third-party items only when the specific record's license/rights supports redistribution; preserve provenance, restrictions and SHA-256.

bundling_policy.allow_automatic: Original assets created by this repository; item-level CC0/verified Public Domain records; NASA-origin media only under its distinct official media-use guidance after restrictive metadata filters; every third-party item keeps its source and rights basis.
bundling_policy.deny_automatic: Non-commercial, no-derivatives, royalty-free marketplace, stock-site, unknown, conflicting, or mixed-license items unless item-level rights explicitly permit redistribution of the file itself. NASA media is not labelled CC0.
bundling_policy.review: A public-domain mark from a third-party aggregator is not automatically proof of status in every jurisdiction; CC0 is preferred for automatic bundling.

sources.title: Godot SplashScreens — Kenney-created CC0 derivative logos only
sources.category: 4K splash screens, reimagined Godot branding, cog logos, text logos
sources.license: Scoped mixed-license repository: only Kenney-created Reimagined, Cog and Text logo paths are CC0-1.0; original Godot logo is CC-BY-4.0
sources.authentication: None; public official GitHub repository archive
sources.note: The repository README says the original Godot logo is CC-BY-4.0, while other derivative logos (reimagined logo, cog logo, text logo) made by Kenney are CC0 licensed. This importer includes only Logo/reimagined*, Logo/text*, Screen/Cog logo/, Screen/Reimagined logo/ and Screen/Text logo/. It excludes Screen/Original logo/ and Logo/original* (CC-BY-4.0), plus Pixel and Pride folders whose rights are not explicitly marked CC0. The repo-level MIT LICENSE covers code, not artwork; the README's explicit per-folder statement is used as the media-rights evidence.

sources.title: NASA Image and Video Library — screened images, video and audio
sources.category: space, astronomy, Earth science, climate, aeronautics
sources.license: NASA Media Usage Guidelines; generally not copyrighted in the United States, but not CC0
sources.note: Only records attributed to NASA centers are considered. Explicit copyright/third-party-rights markers, NASA logos/seals, and obvious identifiable-person keyword categories are skipped. Every bundled record preserves source/media URL and rights basis. Credit NASA, do not imply endorsement, avoid protected insignia, and review privacy/publicity rights before commercial or promotional use.

sources.title: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio — public-domain science visualization videos
sources.kind: official science visualization and moving-image archive
sources.category: Earth science, climate, oceans, hurricanes, astronomy, planetary science, spacecraft, solar activity, aurora and scientific data visualization
sources.license: NASA SVS public-domain default unless otherwise noted; not CC0
sources.note: Uses official NASA SVS Search/Page APIs across topic queries. Preserves title, description, dimensions, dates, creator/employer credits, datasets, science categories, missions, keywords, source page and exact video URL. Only complete studio=SVS pages are considered. HTTP media links are upgraded to HTTPS only on the exact svs.gsfc.nasa.gov /vis/ path; redirects, MIME/container signatures, byte ceilings and SHA-256 are verified. Pages with explicit licensed-music/copyright/permission notes or non-empty audio_track metadata are skipped pending a safe silent variant. NASA SVS says visualizations are public domain unless otherwise noted and that visuals with licensed music may be used without their associated audio tracks. Credit NASA SVS; do not imply endorsement or use insignia as a logo; review privacy/publicity and third-party data before commercial/promotional use.

sources.title: European Southern Observatory — public astronomy and science videos
sources.kind: official video archive and RSS feeds
sources.category: astronomy, exoplanets, galaxies, observatories, telescopes, space science and ESO research
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 default for ESO public videos unless the individual page states otherwise; music excluded unless separately covered
sources.note: Discover pages only through six verified official ESO RSS category feeds (ESOcast, cosmology, exoplanets, fulldome, stars and galaxies). Each individual page must contain a full credit block and a direct checksum-published H.264 4K or 1080p preview. Only exact cdn.eso.org preview URLs are allowed; verify the source SHA-256 published on the item page, MIME/container signature, redirects and byte ceilings. FFmpeg remuxes only the video stream and ffprobe verifies zero audio streams because ESO music is not automatically covered by the general CC BY grant. Preserve the complete credit wording (HTML formatting/whitespace may be normalized in metadata) and require it visibly and unaltered in the finished video; a description-only credit is insufficient. Fail closed on NoDerivatives, non-commercial, permission-required or other restrictive page-specific terms. ESO branding/logo and endorsement restrictions still apply. Disclose that audio was removed when adapting the footage. ESO states commercial use is not permitted if identifiable people appear, so this restriction is surfaced as a mandatory human review flag. Files are CC BY 4.0 default, not CC0.

sources.note: The builder queries a fixed set of 20 official family directories. sources.title: OpenMoji 17.0 — color/black SVG and PNG emoji/sticker artwork
sources.category: reaction emoji, expressive symbols, UI stickers, illustrations and caption overlays
sources.attribution_text: All emojis designed by OpenMoji – the open-source emoji and icon project. License: CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.video_attribution_guidance: The official OpenMoji FAQ recommends attribution in the video description and/or end credits, voice track or a footnote when the first OpenMoji appears.
sources.note: Pinned npm package openmoji@17.0.0. The builder verifies the npm registry version, CC-BY-SA-4.0 license label, official tarball URL, SHA-1 shasum and SHA-512 integrity before extracting only color/black SVG, 618x618 PNG and 72x72 PNG artwork plus central metadata. JavaScript/build code is excluded; SVGs are sanitized and PNG signatures checked. Each file carries its own SHA-256 and CC BY-SA license provenance. Commercial use is permitted with appropriate attribution; indicate changes, and any adapted artwork must remain under CC BY-SA 4.0. Full LICENSE.txt and official FAQ are retained with the resource set.

sources.title: NOAA Ocean Exploration Multimedia — deep-ocean images and videos with caption/credit screening
sources.category: ocean, climate, storms, weather, marine science and research vessels
sources.license: Public Domain by default for NOAA Ocean Exploration site content unless otherwise noted; items with the word copyright in caption/credit/alt or missing NOAA credit are skipped
sources.note: Build 47 raises listing discovery to 20 pages and successful downloads to at most 200 images and 120 videos, with an 8 GiB aggregate ceiling. It still requires an explicit NOAA Credit field, skips a copyright marker in caption/credit/alt text, screens possible identifiable-person/interview contexts, downloads only official item Download URLs, and retains caption, credit, source, metadata and SHA-256.

sources.title: Internet Archive — Prelinger and NASA public-domain/CC0 moving images
sources.category: Historical educational films, industrial/science footage, NASA mission and spaceflight moving images
sources.license: CC0-1.0 or CC0-3.0 from exact item licenseurl; for Prelinger, the legacy item-page Public Domain usage label is separately verified and recorded as Public Domain (not CC0)
sources.note: Search is restricted to the Prelinger and NASA collections and mediatype=movies; the collection itself never grants reuse rights. The exact item metadata must confirm the identifier, mediatype, requested collection and an approved CC0 declaration. Prelinger records whose IA metadata omits the separate rights field may be accepted only when the canonical https://archive.org/details/{identifier} item page has exactly one Usage definition-list entry, whose visible text and linked title are exactly Public Domain and whose rel=license URL is the expected legacy IA Public Domain URL. This is recorded as item-page Public Domain status, never relabelled CC0. A non-empty conflicting rights field, multiple Usage rows, alternate rights label, wrong URL, missing page, or redirect fails closed. This handles legacy Prelinger records such as TillItHe1959 while preserving page-specific verification. Only MP4/WebM/OGV files no larger than 250 MiB with a valid 5–1800 second item duration are downloaded. File MIME/container signature and MD5/SHA-1 are checked against the exact IA file record when supplied; SHA-256 is always stored. Prelinger PDM records may still contain third-party music, archival inserts, identifiable people or other non-copyright rights; these require human review before commercial/promotional use. The lane reserves separate 4 GiB aggregate budgets for Prelinger and NASA (8 GiB combined), with at most 120 items and 250 MiB per file in either collection. A collection cannot consume the other collection's reserved byte budget. These are ceilings, not promised totals.

sources.title: ambientCG — CC0 PBR materials, HDRIs, models, decals, atlases and creative tools
sources.category: PBR surfaces, tileable textures, HDRI lighting environments, 3D models, decals, atlases, plain textures, brushes and Substance materials
sources.license: CC0-1.0 for downloadable ambientCG asset files
sources.note: Build 47 raises the aggregate downloaded-and-extracted content ceiling to 5 GiB and package discovery limits to 140 across Material, HDRI, 3DModel, Decal, Atlas, PlainTexture, Brush and Substance. Downloads remain restricted to official HTTPS /get ZIP endpoints, validated ZIP integrity, allow-listed extraction and source/archive/per-file SHA-256.

sources.title: LazyTextures — CC0 materials, models, HDRIs and texture packs
sources.kind: public 3D asset API and downloadable archive library
sources.category: 3D models, PBR materials, HDRI environment lighting, texture maps and decals
sources.license: CC0-1.0 — official API documentation states all library assets are CC0 1.0
sources.authentication: No API key required for documented public endpoints
sources.note: The importer uses the official previewsModels, previewsMaterials, previewsHDRIs and previewsTextures endpoints, then matches each item by exact name/type against its official /Asset/{type}/{name} detail response. The provider's API documentation states that all library assets are CC0 1.0. Any contradictory item license metadata is rejected. Only ZIP files listed in archiveFiles or textureFiles and served from the exact HTTPS lazytextures.net:3000 /Assets/ path are considered; standalone non-ZIP texture paths are skipped by this archive-only importer. Per-file maximum 64 MiB, 512 MiB total downloaded archives, 128 MiB extracted bytes per item, 1.5 GiB extracted bytes total, and 2,500 ZIP members per archive. Discovery ceilings: 10 models, 16 materials, 10 HDRIs, 18 texture archives and 8 other/miscellaneous packages (62 maximum); per archive 64 MiB, 512 MiB total compressed, 128 MiB unpacked per archive and 1.5 GiB total unpacked. ZIP path/member/size/compression-ratio/CRC preflight occurs before extraction; extracted media passes format-signature checks and SVG sanitization. Requests are paced because downloads are subject to fair-use limits.

sources.title: Poly Pizza — item-verified CC0 low-poly GLB models
sources.kind: low-poly 3D model catalogue and published API
sources.category: 3D models, low-poly nature, characters, buildings, vehicles, furniture, props and environments
sources.license: Per-model Creative Commons licence; this importer accepts exact CC0 1.0 only
sources.authentication: Optional POLY_PIZZA_API_KEY GitHub Actions secret; key is sent only to api.poly.pizza
sources.note: Poly Pizza lists 10,700+ models, but licensing is per model and may vary (CC0 and CC-BY are both present). This importer uses the published API only (no HTML scraping), re-fetches each chosen model by ID, and downloads only a model whose own Licence field is exactly recognized as CC0 1.0. CC-BY, unknown and missing licence records are skipped. The direct GLB URL must be HTTPS on poly.pizza or a subdomain; only GLB v2 with a matching declared length is indexed. Limits: 48 models, 128 MiB per GLB and 4 GiB total. The API key is never forwarded to the asset CDN. The provider's Terms prohibit scraping/automated extraction outside published interfaces; this lane uses the published API. Check the current account plan/terms before enabling commercial use: the provider's press page has described API access as free for hobby use and pay-as-you-go for commercial use. Search discovery is bounded to two pages per term and 240 unique CC0 candidates before downloading at most 48 models. The GLB must be an HTTPS .glb URL, contain a valid GLB v2 JSON chunk, have no remote/sidecar URIs, and pass binary chunk and buffer-length validation. Output folder names include a SHA-256 ID suffix to avoid case-insensitive path collisions.

sources.title: Quaternius — 3D packs for use in finished products (not raw library redistribution)
sources.category: Low-poly characters, environments, props, nature and animated game assets
sources.license: Quaternius Asset License (QAL) v1.0 — standalone asset redistribution prohibited
sources.note: The current official QAL v1.0 allows use, modification and incorporation into finished products including films and games, but prohibits reselling, repackaging, sublicensing or otherwise redistributing the assets themselves, in original or modified form, as standalone assets, asset packs, stock files, templates or similar products, whether alone or bundled with other assets. This repository is a downloadable raw asset library, so current-QAL files are not imported. Some legacy pack pages/older FAQ copies may still say CC0; do not assume that site-wide or apply the old FAQ to new downloads. Only consider a historical pack for bundling after checking its own dated license evidence and applicability. Source: https://quaternius.com/license.html; legacy FAQ: https://quaternius.com/faq.html.

sources.title: Original in-repository procedural motion loops
sources.category: technology, science, atmosphere, retro, documentary, music and abstract transitions
sources.note: The build generates 12 six-second 1280×720 H.264 loops from FFmpeg filter graphs; no external footage, imagery or audio are embedded. Each output is verified with ffprobe for codec, dimensions and duration, and the file receives a SHA-256 digest in the asset manifest. These are illustrative loops, not factual footage.

sources.title: Original Nolane sticker, reaction, meme-layout and caption template packs
sources.category: reaction stickers, meme layouts, lower thirds, title cards, source notes, subtitles and social CTAs
sources.note: All items are original vector layouts generated by this repository. They are generic editable sticker/meme layouts and caption overlays, not copies of copyrighted characters, brand marks or famous meme-image templates. Replace text placeholders and use only footage or photos you have rights to.

sources.title: National Archives Catalog — AWS Registry of Open Data (research-only candidate)
sources.kind: public bulk archival metadata and digital-object catalogue
sources.category: historical motion pictures, military and aviation footage, photographs, sound recordings and video
sources.license: AWS Registry listing labels the dataset as a US Government work; each digitized media item must still pass its own NARA use-restriction, access-restriction and third-party-rights checks
sources.authentication: Public AWS S3 dataset access is documented with --no-sign-request; do not use the NARA Catalog API for bulk cache/download because its API terms separately prohibit storing API-returned content and require API keys
sources.note: NARA states the AWS dataset contains more than 148 million digital-object URLs and its full catalog export is over 261 GB; the descriptions export is distributed in record-group and collection directories, each JSON file containing up to 10,000 descriptions. Promising candidate record groups include RG 111 (Army Signal Corps motion pictures), RG 342 (Air Force motion pictures/video) and RG 428 (Naval Photographic Center motion pictures). Before any media is downloaded, the importer must parse the exact record-level useRestriction.status and require Unrestricted, separately parse accessRestriction.status and require Unrestricted, verify that digital object files are publicly downloadable and audiovisual, then retain the record NAID/title, file-level source URL, rights notes and SHA-256. Unrestricted means no recorded copyright, donor or other use restrictions; it is not a blanket waiver of privacy, publicity, third-party, classified or other rights. The API terms prohibit storing content returned by the Catalog API; prefer the separately distributed AWS dataset only after validating its actual JSON schema and dataset conditions. This entry is research-only and contributes zero bytes until an importer passes the rights gate.
